significance.value: 99.95% CL (deficit inconsistent with standard ν̄e propagation)

summary.plain: KamLAND's first data showed fewer antineutrinos from distant Japanese reactors than expected (observed/expected 0.611). The deficit is inconsistent with standard antineutrino propagation at the 99.95% confidence level; assuming two-flavor oscillations with CPT invariance, only the 'Large Mixing Angle' solution to the solar neutrino problem remains.
summary.technical: In a 162 ton·yr (145.1-day) exposure, KamLAND measured a ratio of observed to expected reactor antineutrino events of 0.611 ± 0.085(stat) ± 0.041(syst) for E > 3.4 MeV; the deficit is inconsistent with the expected rate for standard ν̄e propagation at the 99.95% confidence level, and in the context of two-flavor neutrino oscillations with CPT invariance the results exclude all oscillation solutions but the 'Large Mixing Angle' solution to the solar neutrino problem.

title: First Results from KamLAND: Evidence for Reactor Anti-Neutrino Disappearance

why_it_matters.quote: these results exclude all oscillation solutions but the ‘Large Mixing Angle’ solution to the solar neutrino problem using reactor ν̄e sources
why_it_matters.value: In the context of two-flavor oscillations with CPT invariance, the first KamLAND data exclude every oscillation solution to the solar neutrino problem except the Large Mixing Angle solution, using reactor antineutrinos.
